q: A horn in F reads a written C. What sounds?
why: Horn in F sounds a P5 below written.

q: A B♭ clarinet reads a written D. What sounds?
why: B♭ instruments sound a major 2nd below written.

q: To have a B♭ trumpet sound concert C, write…
why: Write a major 2nd higher than you want to hear.

q: An E♭ alto saxophone sounds how far from what it reads?
why: Written C sounds the E♭ below.

q: An A clarinet reads a written C. What sounds?
why: Instruments in A sound a minor 3rd below written.

q: Which instrument sounds an octave higher than written?
why: Piccolo, xylophone and celesta are written lower than they sound.

q: Which instrument sounds an octave lower than written?
why: Guitar, contrabass and contrabassoon are written an octave higher than they sound.

q: A tenor saxophone in B♭ sounds…
why: It's the B♭ transposition plus an octave.

a: every part as it sounds, apart from octave-transposing instruments
w: every part as the players read it
why: Piccolo, double bass and similar instruments usually keep their octave transposition.
